input:
## Basis
This report is concerned with the design of a distillation column, the purpose of which is to separate a liquid feed into two products, namely an overhead product and a bottoms product. The design throughput of the column is 32 t per day of feed. The separation duty that is called for is 90% of the key component present in the feed, taken overhead, so that the overhead product contains that share of the key component, while the bottoms contains the balance, together with the heavier components of the feed. All wetted parts are manufactured in 316L stainless steel, and the grade is stated once, at this point; the materials section of the report proceeds on the basis of this statement. The column operates continuously at the design throughput. The feed is introduced at the feed stage, vapour rises up the column against liquid flowing downwards, and the separation is effected by repeated contact between the two phases on the stages that are situated between the feed stage and the ends of the column. A condenser at the top of the column returns a part of the overhead vapour in the form of reflux and sends the remainder to product, and a reboiler at the bottom returns a part of the bottoms in the form of vapour and sends the remainder to product. The basis thus establishes the rate and the duty, and such matters as the number of stages, the reflux rate, the diameter of the column and the pressure level at which the separation is carried out are dealt with in the sizing section.
## Sizing
The sizing of the column takes as its starting point the design throughput of 32 t per day and the separation duty of 90% of the key component taken overhead. The number of stages is determined by the separation that the duty requires. Each stage brings the vapour and the liquid into contact with one another and moves the key component in the direction of the overhead product; the stages above the feed serve to enrich the vapour in the key component, and the stages below the feed serve to strip the key component out of the liquid that is running down to the bottoms. The count of stages is built up from the equilibrium behaviour of the mixture, stage by stage, and the feed stage is located at the position where the composition of the feed corresponds to the composition of the liquid on the stage, so that the introduction of the feed does not disturb the traffic in either section of the column. The reflux rate is fixed in conjunction with the stage count: a higher rate of reflux sharpens the separation that is achieved on each stage and reduces the number of stages that the duty requires, although this is at the price of a larger traffic of vapour and liquid within the column and a larger duty at the condenser and at the reboiler. The diameter of the column is determined by the traffic of vapour. The vapour that rises through the column and the liquid that runs down it share the cross-section of the column, and the diameter is selected in such a way that the vapour rate at the busiest section remains below the rate at which liquid begins to be carried upwards with the vapour and the stages cease to perform their separation. The condenser and the reboiler are sized on the basis of the traffic that results from the choice of reflux: the condenser deals with the whole of the overhead vapour, condensing both the part that is returned as reflux and the part that is sent to product, and the reboiler raises from the bottoms liquid the vapour that the column requires. The pressure drop is summed stage by stage through the column and is checked against the pressure level at which the column works, because the pressure determines the temperatures at which the two products condense and boil. The sizing concludes with a check of the column operating at the design rate.
## Materials
All wetted parts are manufactured in the stainless steel grade that has been named in the basis. The shell of the column, the stages together with their fittings, the feed inlet, the overhead line to the condenser, the condenser itself, the reflux return, the bottoms outlet and the reboiler are all in contact with the feed, with the products or with the liquids in the column, and the grade applies to each and every one of them. The liquids in the column represent the aggressive streams from the point of view of material selection: the feed wets the feed stage and the section below it on a continuous basis, the reflux wets the top section, and the bottoms liquid stands hot in the sump and in the reboiler, where a weakness in the material will show itself first in the form of attack at the heated surface. The fittings of the stages are subject to a second kind of service, in that they are handled at every shutdown and are removed and replaced during cleaning and inspection, and their material must therefore be able to withstand that handling as well as the process liquid. Small parts, such as downcomer bolts and stage fasteners, are held to the grade of the parts that they join, since a fastener manufactured in a weaker material may well fail in a crevice into which the inspection cannot see. Surfaces that are in product contact are finished in such a way that deposits can be cleaned off at a shutdown and do not lodge underneath the stages. Gaskets at the joints of the shell and at the connections of the condenser and the reboiler are selected for the liquids in the column and for the cleaning fluids that are used at shutdown.
## Risks
There are two items which remain open in the design, namely fouling and turndown, and it has to be said that neither of these items is resolved in this report. Fouling has a direct effect on the separation itself. Deposits are formed on the stages at the points where the feed enters and where any heavy material in the feed is able to settle, and a stage that has become fouled no longer brings the vapour and the liquid into contact in the manner that the sizing assumes: the liquid channels across the deposit, the vapour finds the open paths, and the stage delivers a smaller separation than its design value. Fouling also has the effect of narrowing the downcomers, with the result that the traffic of liquid for which the diameter was set cannot pass, and the column floods at a rate below its design rate. The design provides access for cleaning at the feed section and at the bottom of the column, and records the fouling rate of the feed as the quantity that is required at the next stage; until such time as that rate is known, no cleaning interval is stated. Turndown is the second of the open items. At rates below the design throughput, the rate of vapour falls, and the stages depend upon the vapour in order to hold the liquid up and to bring about the contact that the separation requires; at a sufficiently low rate of vapour the liquid weeps through the stages instead of flowing across them, and the separation deteriorates more rapidly than the rate itself. The reflux control maintains the compositions of the products over a part of the range, but the lower end of the range is determined by the behaviour of the stages and not by the controls. Both items are accordingly recorded for attention at the next design stage.

## Basis
The design covers a distillation column that separates a liquid feed into an overhead product and a bottoms product. The design throughput is 32 t per day of feed. The separation duty is 90% of the key component in the feed, taken overhead: the overhead product carries that share of the key component, and the bottoms carries the balance together with the heavier components of the feed. Wetted parts are 316L stainless steel, and the basis states the grade once, here; the materials section works from this statement. The column works continuously at the design throughput. Feed enters the column at the feed stage, vapour rises against liquid flowing down, and the separation is made by repeated contact between the two phases on the stages between the feed stage and the ends of the column. A condenser at the top returns part of the overhead vapour as reflux and sends the rest to product; a reboiler at the bottom returns part of the bottoms as vapour and sends the rest to product. The basis fixes the rate and the duty. The number of stages, the reflux rate, the column diameter and the pressure level of the separation are set in the sizing section, and the basis does not prejudge them. The two products are drawn continuously, and the column inventories are held by level control at the sump and at the reflux return.
## Sizing
Sizing starts from the design throughput of 32 t per day and the separation duty of 90% of the key component taken overhead. The stage count is set by the separation the duty demands. Each stage brings vapour and liquid into contact and moves the key component towards the overhead product; the stages above the feed enrich the vapour in the key component, and the stages below the feed strip the key component out of the liquid running to the bottoms. The count is built up from the equilibrium behaviour of the mixture stage by stage, and the feed stage is placed where the feed composition matches the liquid on the stage, so the feed enters without disturbing the traffic in either section. The reflux rate is set with the stage count: a higher reflux rate sharpens the separation on each stage and lowers the stage count the duty needs, at the price of a larger vapour and liquid traffic in the column and a larger duty at the condenser and the reboiler. The sizing takes the pair of values, stage count and reflux, that meets the duty with the column in steady operation and holds a working margin above the minimum reflux the separation allows. The column diameter is set by the vapour traffic. The vapour rising through the column and the liquid running down share the cross-section, and the diameter is chosen so the vapour rate at the busiest section stays below the rate at which liquid is carried up with the vapour and the stages lose their separation. The section above the feed normally sets the diameter, because the reflux adds to its liquid traffic. Stage spacing is set by the need to separate the phases between stages and to give access for inspection and cleaning. The condenser and reboiler are sized on the traffic the reflux choice creates: the condenser takes the full overhead vapour, condenses the part returned as reflux and the part sent to product, and the reboiler raises the vapour the column needs from the bottoms liquid. Pressure drop is summed stage by stage through the column and checked against the pressure level the basis works at, because the pressure fixes the temperatures at which the two products condense and boil. The sizing closes with a check of the column at the design rate: feed in at the feed stage, overhead and bottoms out at the stated duty, stage traffic steady in both sections.
## Materials
Wetted parts are the stainless steel grade named in the basis. The column shell, the stages and their fittings, the feed inlet, the overhead line to the condenser, the condenser itself, the reflux return, the bottoms outlet and the reboiler all stand in contact with the feed, the products or the column liquids, and the grade is applied to each of them. The liquids in the column are the aggressive streams for material selection: the feed wets the feed stage and the section below it continuously, the reflux wets the top section, and the bottoms liquid stands hot in the sump and in the reboiler, where a material weakness shows first as attack at the heated surface. Stage fittings take a second kind of service: they are handled at every shutdown, removed and replaced during cleaning and inspection, and their material has to stand that handling as well as the process liquid. Small parts, downcomer bolts and stage fasteners are held to the grade of the parts they join, because a fastener of a weaker material fails in a crevice the inspection cannot see into. Surfaces in product contact are finished so that deposits can be cleaned off at a shutdown and do not lodge under the stages. Gaskets at the shell joints and at the condenser and reboiler connections are selected for the column liquids and for the cleaning fluids used at shutdown. The materials section adds no second statement of the grade: a part listed as wetted is governed by the basis statement.
## Risks
Fouling and turndown stand as open items in the design, and neither is resolved in this report. Fouling acts on the separation directly. Deposits form on the stages where the feed enters and where any heavy material in the feed can settle, and a fouled stage no longer contacts vapour and liquid as the sizing assumes: liquid channels across the deposit, vapour finds the open paths, and the stage delivers less separation than its design value. Fouling also narrows the downcomers, so the liquid traffic the diameter was set for cannot pass, and the column floods below its design rate. The design leaves access for cleaning at the feed section and the bottom of the column and records the fouling rate of the feed as the quantity the next stage needs; until that rate is known, no cleaning interval is stated and no spare capacity is claimed against fouling. Turndown is the second open item. Below the design throughput the vapour rate falls, and the stages depend on the vapour to hold the liquid up and to make the contact the separation needs; at a low enough vapour rate the liquid weeps through the stages instead of flowing across them, and the separation falls away faster than the rate does. The reflux control holds the product compositions over part of the range, but the lower end of the range is set by the stage behaviour, not by the controls. The report records the turndown item for the next design stage: it closes when the stage behaviour at reduced vapour rate is confirmed for the stage type selected, and the fouling item closes when a deposit rate for the feed is available from operation or test.
